question: A 24-year-old woman comes to the physician for a routine pelvic examination. She feels well. Menses occur at 30-day intervals and last 7 days. Her last menstrual period was 6 days ago. She has no history of abnormal Pap smears; her last Pap smear was 13 months ago. She is sexually active with three male partners and uses condoms consistently. She has never been tested for sexually transmitted infections. Her 54-year-old mother has breast cancer. She is up-to-date on her Tdap, MMR, and varicella vaccinations. Her temperature is 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse is 68/min, and blood pressure is 108/68 mm Hg. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. In addition to HIV, gonorrhea, and chlamydia testing, which of the following is the most appropriate recommendation at this time?
analysis: The patient is a 24-year-old woman who is sexually active with multiple partners and has never been tested for sexually transmitted infections. In addition to testing for HIV, gonorrhea, and chlamydia, it is important to consider her risk factors for HPV, especially given her sexual history. The HPV vaccination is recommended for women up to age 26, and since she is 24, she is still eligible for vaccination. Therefore, the most appropriate recommendation at this time is to offer HPV vaccination.
